text.p: Telecommunications company Intermedia Communications said Thursday it had signed a definitive agreement to buy DIGEX Inc for $13 a share, or about $150 million.
Intermedia said in a statement the shareholders owning a majority stake in DIGEX, an Internet provider, had agreed to the takeover.
Intermedia said it will make a tender offer for all outstanding DIGEX shares next week and later conduct a cash merger.
It said it will give DIGEX management and other option holders Intermedia stock options, rather than cash, for their DIGEX stock options.
The deal should close in the third quarter, it added.
"The resulting third quarter EBITDA for the combined company is expected to be within the current range of analysts' expectations for Intermedia," it said.
"This acquisition should accelerate our progression toward positive cash flow and adds meaningfully to EBITDA beginning in 1998," it added.
Intermedia said it expected to realize minimum cost savings of about $4 million in the second half of 1997, $12 million in 1998, $14 million in 1999, "and increasing savings in subsequent years".
According to First Call, the consensus among analysts is that Intermedia will lose $2.50 a share for the second quarter and $2.43 for the third quarter.
About 75 percent of DIGEX's backbone network overlaps existing or planned Intermedia network routes, Intermedia said.
